findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The PIC could not produce proof of food handler’s certificate. Ensure that all employees that handle food are food handler certified if not a food protection manager. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the interior cavities of the microwave to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC that the cavities of the microwave should be cleaned as necessary to prevent food contamination. Ensure that the interior of the microwave is cleaned frequently and free of food debris. 

4-602.12: (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Food service employee working in the kitchen has a food handler certification but does not have a food manager certification. Food service employee is the designated person in charge (PIC) as they are the person preparing and handling food, answering questions during inspection, and performing their duties. Information about food manager course was provided for food service employee and director of the facility to obtain certification. Ensure the person working in the kitchen is a certified food manager. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC was observed washing hands without proper technique.  Employee touched handles to dispense paper towels for drying after faucet was shut off. Handwashing signage showing proper technique is posted adjacent to the sink. Ensure proper handwashing technique is used every time hands are washed. Have paper towels dispensed and ready to use and/or use an elbow/forearm to touch handles when shutting off the faucet and dispensing paper towels. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Bleach solution was prepared and observed at a concentration above 200ppm. Test strip was bleached out when used to check concentration. Solution was diluted to 100ppm. Maintain bleach solutions for product being used at 100-200ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.  
Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
There are numerous mouse droppings observed between the cooler and milk cooler, in the cabinet under the hand sink and in the laundry closet. Maintenance has been notified and Springfield Termite (PCO) made a site visit yesterday to address. Clean all of these areas, which will likely include moving refrigerators and washing machines out to clean behind, and monitor for activity while continuing to provide effective pest control. A spot check will be performed in 2 weeks.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
There are numerous holes around the pipes underneath the hand sink and there is a large hole to the right of the washing machine in the laundry closet. Holes need to be filled with a smooth and easily cleanable material. While steel wool is an ideal material to deter pests, it is not smooth and easily cleanable and must be covered with a material that is.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed corn, chicken "o"s  and open canned fruit in the cooler that was not date marked. It was reported that these items are from lunch last Thursday and were discarded during the inspection. Any items that are cooled to hold for reheating at a future date must be marked with the date the items were originally prepared and held no longer than 7 days maximum.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Facility is using pine sol and dish soap to clean food contact surfaces in the kitchen. It was discussed at length during inspection that this is not an approved sanitizer. Cease the use of pine sol on food contact surfaces and begin using bleach or quat solution, which are approved sanitizers.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Pans and pots are behind stored within these soiled cabinets. Keep cabinets clean to protect cleaned and sanitized equipment. Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1130(e) There are two pans (one dry, one with water) beneath the two compartment sink. It appears that the two containers are holding waste water from the 2-comp,. sink plumbing. The dry container (soiled inside with evaporated water, dust, and mold) was discarded. the water from the larger container was disposed of, the container was washed. Proper handling of waste water was discussed. I allowed the water to run and could not observe where the pan water was originating. Dispose of water sources promptly to deter pests from finding a water source.  Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.
